data.title: Fake Mobile App Residential Proxy and Subscription Scam Detection
data.description: Detects indicators of fake mobile applications that function as residential proxies or subscription scams, as documented in the VexTrio fake app operations (Black Hat USA 2025, Infoblox). VexTrio operated fake mobile apps for 7-8 years through Google Play Store, Apple App Store, and third-party forums. Three categories: (1) Fake VPNs that route user traffic through residential proxy networks (making users unwitting proxy nodes) with keyword-scanning capabilities targeting banking and personal information, (2) Fake Android cleaners (device optimization tools), (3) Fake spam/notification protection apps that operate a self-referential scam cycle — after push notification abuse infects the victim browser (100-150 notifications/day), victim is served an ad for a "spam protection" app that requests permissions to disable browser notifications, displays fabricated "blocked" notification screens, then transitions to $6.99/week subscription after 24 hours. This rule detects network-level and endpoint-level indicators of these app categories.

detection.condition: selection_proxy_behavior or selection_keyword_scanning or (selection_notification_abuse_precursor and selection_subscription_scam)

enrichment_required.source: Network traffic analysis (proxy behavior detection via traffic flow analysis)
WHOIS enrichment for push notification source domains

queries.splunk:
`comment("Splunk SPL for Fake Mobile App Residential Proxy and Subscription Scam Detection")`
`comment("Detects VexTrio-pattern fake apps: residential proxy abuse and notification-to-subscription scam cycle")`

`comment("--- Detection 1: Fake VPN acting as residential proxy ---")`
index=flame_endpoint sourcetype=flame:mobile_mdm app_category IN ("VPN", "cleaner", "optimizer", "spam-blocker")
| stats
    dc(dest_ip) AS unique_dest_ips
    sum(bytes_out) AS total_bytes_out
    sum(bytes_in) AS total_bytes_in
    dc(src_port) AS unique_src_ports
    values(app_name) AS app_names
  by device_id, app_id
| eval proxy_ratio=round(total_bytes_in/total_bytes_out, 2)
| where unique_dest_ips > 50 AND proxy_ratio > 2
| eval risk="residential_proxy_behavior"

`comment("--- Detection 2: Push notification abuse to subscription scam cycle ---")`
index=flame_endpoint sourcetype=flame:mobile_mdm
| eval has_notification_spike=(if(push_notification_count_24h >= 50, 1, 0))
| eval has_app_install=(if(isnotnull(new_app_install) AND app_category IN ("spam-blocker", "notification-protector", "cleaner"), 1, 0))
| eval has_subscription=(if(in_app_purchase_amount >= 6.99 AND in_app_purchase_type="subscription", 1, 0))
| transaction device_id maxspan=72h
| where has_notification_spike=1 AND has_app_install=1 AND has_subscription=1
| eval risk="notification_to_subscription_scam_cycle"
queries.sql:
-- SQL for Fake Mobile App Residential Proxy Detection
-- Identifies apps with proxy-like traffic patterns (high inbound/outbound ratio, many destinations)
SELECT
  d.device_id,
  a.app_name,
  a.app_publisher,
  a.app_category,
  COUNT(DISTINCT nc.dest_ip) AS unique_destinations,
  SUM(nc.bytes_out) AS total_bytes_out,
  SUM(nc.bytes_in) AS total_bytes_in,
  ROUND(SUM(nc.bytes_in)::numeric / NULLIF(SUM(nc.bytes_out), 0), 2) AS proxy_ratio,
  a.install_date,
  a.requested_permissions
FROM device_inventory d
JOIN installed_apps a ON d.device_id = a.device_id
JOIN network_connections nc ON d.device_id = nc.device_id AND a.app_id = nc.app_id
WHERE a.app_category IN ('VPN', 'cleaner', 'optimizer', 'spam-blocker', 'notification-protector')
  AND nc.connection_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '7 days'
GROUP BY d.device_id, a.app_name, a.app_publisher, a.app_category,
         a.install_date, a.requested_permissions
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT nc.dest_ip) > 50
   AND ROUND(SUM(nc.bytes_in)::numeric / NULLIF(SUM(nc.bytes_out), 0), 2) > 2.0
ORDER BY unique_destinations DESC;

falsepositives: Legitimate VPN applications with high connection counts (though legitimate VPNs typically connect to known VPN provider infrastructure, not diverse residential IPs)
Enterprise MDM tools that manage notification settings
Legitimate notification management apps from established publishers
